newsitem.title: HAITI: Two more Haitian police killed in crime wave.
newsitem.headline: Two more Haitian police killed in crime wave.

text.p: The bodies of two police officers were found outside the southern city of Petit Goave, bringing to at least five the number of police killed in a recent crime wave, police said on Thursday.

The officers, identified as Ladoucer Beril and Donald Daimant, were found on Wednesday near a highway. Radio Metropole reported that witnesses said the officers were killed by a group of four men and early ballistics evidence suggested they were gunned down with an M-16.
"All we know right now is that they are dead and that they were killed by gunshots," Haitian National Police spokesman Felder Jean-Baptiste said.

According to United Nations sources, six police officers have been killed during a recent wave of violent crime that has gripped Haiti. Published reports say at least 40 people were killed in a two-week period in the capital alone.
Jean-Baptiste said he could only confirm five police officers had been killed and did not have any recent murder rate figures.
The Haitian press has reported eight police officers have been killed, but U.N. sources said that was due to an initial misidentification of two civilian victims as police officers.
